subject: Borealis cutover: intermittent TLS failures + asymmetric routing during NAT switchover
messages:
From: Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: networking-team@borealishealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Hi Vanessa,

We completed the PoP cutover this morning (Equinix NJ). Since ~07:30 our app stack is seeing intermittent 502s and TLS session resets to Redwood endpoints for API traffic originating from our internal services. Healthchecks for the private-deploy frontdoors are flapping: some probes succeed, then subsequent probes show TCP RST or no response.

Scope details:
- Private Redwood deployment (VPC peered) — single NAT gateway (SNAT) was migrated to new egress IPs during the cutover.
- Symptoms: TLS handshake failures, long tail ESTABLISHED->CLOSEW wait for some sessions, and occasional 502s in app logs.
- We've captured a tcpdump and conntrack snapshot attached.

Can Redwood help triage — suspect asymmetric return path or ephemeral port exhaustion on your side after the NAT change. This is impacting production traffic.

Thanks,
Peter Lin
Sr. SRE, Borealis Health
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, equinix-sales@equinix.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Hi Peter — sorry to hear you're seeing this after the cutover. We're treating this as an escalation.

Quick asks so we can prioritize:
1) Can you confirm if the failing requests are all egressing from the new Equinix NJ public IP(es) or a mix (old + new)?
2) Please include a short example of request timestamps + upstream request IDs for any 502s.
3) We'll review the tcpdump/conntrack you attached and run correlation against our frontdoor logs.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa (Networking) will pull frontdoor traces and look for SYN/ACK asymmetry.
- Karthik will review conntrack snapshots and search for SNAT port reuse / exhaustion patterns.

We aim to have a first update within 60 minutes. If you can indicate a low-traffic maintenance window later today, we can schedule NAT sticky mappings or soft-failover to the previous egress as a mitigation.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>, networking-team@borealishealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Quick triage notes (what I pulled from our edge traces):
- We see a subset of client IPs in NJ with a high rate of TCP retransmits and duplicated SYNs.
- For affected flows the frontend (Redwood edge) completed TLS ServerHello but application-layer errors followed quickly — consistent with either (a) asymmetric return path dropping ESTABLISHED packets, or (b) early NAT port collision leading to responses mapped to the wrong tuple.
- No firewall drops recorded on our edge but our LB logs show healthcheck fail counts increased right around the cutover window (07:28–07:45).

What I want to collect from Borealis (if possible):
- Exact client source IPs (examples) that correlate to failing sessions.
- Whether Borealis applied any SNAT port-range changes or port-preserving behavior during the cutover.

Attachments: conntrack_snapshot.txt (from Borealis) — initial look: many ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT but also a couple of lines with repeated translations pointing at small ephemeral-port entropy. Could be port re-use under heavy flow churn.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Networking Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Vanessa / Marissa — thanks for the quick look. A few notes from our side:
- All failing requests we sampled are egressing from the new Equinix NJ IP block: 198.51.100.240/29 (we're still deprecating the old block).
- We did not change SNAT port-range intentionally — using vendor default (1024-65535). We do see high connection churn from our ephemeral microservices.
- Attached pcap shows SYN -> SYN/ACK -> ACK followed by application data, then shortly after a RST coming back from the client side (we see the server send application data that the client says is for an _other_ session).

We can schedule a short maintenance window at 19:00 PST tonight for any remediation. If there's a config you want us to toggle (MSS clamping / lowering initial TTL / adjust source port policy) we can coordinate.

Peter
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>
Cc: equinix-sales@equinix.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Summary of findings after correlating pcap + conntrack + edge logs:
- Not a pure MTU issue. Packets are not being fragmented in normal cases; no ICMP PMTU errors seen.
- Evidence points to SNAT port aliasing under heavy churn: we observed (in conntrack) short-lived translations where the same NAT port was reused for different 5-tuples within <200ms. When the return path used a different egress (split-horizon during cutover), the return packets landed at the wrong NAT mapping and produced RSTs on the client side.
- Additionally, a small subset of flows show asymmetric egress/return via a legacy peering path (old PoP) for background monitoring systems — this explains why only some clients saw failures.

Proposed mitigations (we should coordinate during your 19:00 PST window):
1) Redwood: apply temporary SNAT sticky mapping for Borealis public IPs — preserve 1:1 port affinity for 30 minutes to drain churn. (Action: Redwood infra ops)
2) Borealis: enable short-term MSS clamp to 1400 on the egress path to remove any remaining fragmentation risk (Action: Borealis infra)
3) Joint: schedule a 10-minute rolling failback to older egress path for persistent flows if errors continue (Action: joint runbook).

If Equinix needs to confirm routing propagation at their fabric, we loop them. This should be low-risk and reversible.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lin <ops@borealishealth.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: equinix-sales@equinix.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures after cutover to new PoP — seeing 502s and TLS resets

Follow-up / agreed plan (post-testing):
- At 19:05 PST we applied temporary SNAT sticky mappings for the Borealis egress CIDR (198.51.100.240/29) on Redwood's private frontdoors. Observed error rate dropped ~92% within 6 minutes; healthchecks stabilized.
- Borealis applied MSS clamp to 1400 as suggested — no PMTU regressions after clamp.
- We validated no firewall or SG rules at Redwood blocked return path — logs show responses delivered and acknowledged for previously failing flows.
- Action items:
  * (Redwood) Transition sticky mapping to a short TTL (5 minutes) and monitor for 24 hours — Action owner: Marissa.
  * (Borealis) Review ephemeral port socket churn patterns with app teams; consider connection pooling to reduce SNAT pressure — Action owner: Peter.
  * (Joint) Create a permanent runbook for PoP cutovers that includes TTL ramp for BGP announcements and a pre-cutover SNAT port-capacity check — Action owner: Vanessa.

Files stored: pcap + conntrack snapshots are in the shared drive link above. Closing the immediate incident as mitigated; will keep thread open for runbook and postmortem.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
